title: heare Phase B — Prompt hardening + tool allowlist
notes: Two defects from the original research: D1 (generator prompt is underspecified — Gemini Flash Lite guesses wrong args or emits intent for passive mentions like 'gmail.com') and D5 (IntentQueue.submit accepts any tool string, so a bogus tool would silently no-op at the Claude SDK layer). Narrow and concrete — change one prompt file and one queue method.

stories.title: Generator prompt schema + examples + don't-emit rule
stories.description: Rewrite the INTENTS section of prompts/generator.txt to (a) declare a strict JSON schema with tool='bash' as the ONLY allowed value, (b) expand the trigger-verb list to cover common Ukrainian imperatives, (c) provide 3 concrete positive examples and 2 negative examples, (d) include an explicit 'if unsure, just speak' fallback rule, and (e) list a short forbidden-commands note (rm -rf, sudo, curl | bash). Do NOT rewrite the rest of the template; keep existing placeholders and reply rules intact.
acceptanceCriteria: prompts/generator.txt still contains all existing placeholders: {persona}, {time}, {timezone}, {recent_transcripts}, {conversation_summary}, {active_topics}, {entities}, {recent_turns}, {recent_actions}, {transcript}. Test asserts exact placeholder set.
prompts/generator.txt contains the string 'tool' and the string '"bash"' — a strict schema block that names bash as the sole allowed tool.

prompts/generator.txt contains at least 3 positive intent examples (different commands like echo, ls/pwd, open -a) and at least 2 negative examples (user utterance that should NOT produce an intent — e.g. 'gmail.com' alone or 'хочу відкрити щось').
prompts/generator.txt contains a 'якщо не впевнений — не додавай intent' (or equivalent Ukrainian phrase) fallback rule.
prompts/generator.txt contains a forbidden-patterns warning mentioning at least 'rm -rf' and 'sudo' — model must refuse / speak instead.
New test in tests/test_generator_prompt.py asserts each of the above (5 assertions).
test_template_has_exactly_expected_placeholders keeps passing — no placeholders added or removed.

stories.title: IntentQueue enforces tool allowlist and args length
stories.description: IntentQueue.submit currently accepts any non-empty tool string and any args length. Add: tool must be in ALLOWED_TOOLS = {'bash'}; args length must be <= MAX_ARGS_LEN = 2000. Rejections log a specific warning and return None (same as current queue-full rejection path).
acceptanceCriteria: src/actions.py defines module-level ALLOWED_TOOLS: set[str] = {'bash'} and MAX_ARGS_LEN: int = 2000.
IntentQueue.submit rejects payloads whose tool is not in ALLOWED_TOOLS with a '[INTENT REJECTED — tool not allowed tool=X]' warning and returns None.
IntentQueue.submit rejects payloads whose args exceed MAX_ARGS_LEN with a '[INTENT REJECTED — args too long len=N]' warning and returns None.
Empty-tool rejection keeps its existing warning text for backward compat.

New unit tests in tests/test_actions.py: (a) non-allowed tool returns None + warning, (b) args too long returns None + warning, (c) bash + short args still accepted (smoke test). Use caplog at WARNING level.
Existing action tests still pass (all submit calls use tool='bash' with short args).
